feed.title: RSS System Design Articles
feed.subtitle: System design decisions, architectures and failures from engineering blogs. Summaries and Classifier leverages AI; may contain errors.

entry.title: 4 real? Tracking exploitation and patching of eMudhra’s weak keys
entry.summary: Failure analysis of eMudhra intermediate CA keys recoverable from public certificates, covering how Cloudflare patched Pingora within hours, logged about 22,000 weak-key handshakes, and probed client trust through challenge pages.

entry.title: Overhauling DoorDash’s Runtime Configuration Value Distribution with SquashFS
entry.summary: Shows the design decision to replace eager .tar.gz extraction of tens of thousands of config files on every Kubernetes node with on-demand SquashFS loop mounts, cutting extraction latency over 100x and EBS IOPS over 5x.

entry.title: When the Kubernetes API went silent: A three-layer networking mystery
entry.summary: Failure analysis of GKE pods timing out to the API server, traced to a Private Service Connect change dropping RFC 5961 challenge ACKs, packet reordering, Envoy half-close and a Linux kernel 6.1 FIN-handling bug.

entry.title: From synthetic enterprise data evaluations to real Microsoft Copilot AI confidence
entry.summary: Architecture walkthrough of a platform generating synthetic enterprise tenants grounded in occupational data, job postings and SEC filings plus a six-stage query pipeline, a design driven by the constraint that no customer data be used.

entry.title: Build a Validated Kubernetes Runtime for NVIDIA Dynamo
entry.summary: Architecture walkthrough of NVIDIA Dynamo's Kubernetes runtime, comparing the Dynamo Frontend router with the Gateway API and EPP path for KV-cache-aware routing, and why live KV events are used instead of predicted cache state.

entry.title: An agent or a committee? What using committees has taught me since setting them up (translated from French)
entry.summary: Shows the decision to use one agent with escalation and a script verifier instead of agent committees, after a committee cost 4.3 times more tokens and the agent verifier wrongly accepted 8 of 44 proofs.

entry.title: Designing a Generalized Ads Marketplace Platform
entry.summary: Shows the design decisions behind the Uber generalized ads marketplace, including supply, marketplace and demand separation, the AdSpec abstraction, extension-based requests, page-level APIs and config-defined isolated fleets sharing one codebase.

entry.title: How BMW Group accelerated connected vehicle workloads on AWS Graviton
entry.summary: Shows the migration decisions for moving the BMW Connected Vehicle platform to Graviton, including native versus QEMU-emulated multi-arch builds, tainted opt-in Karpenter node pools and x86 fallback, saving about 600,000 dollars annually.

entry.title: How boAt delivers personalized fitness coaching with Amazon Bedrock
entry.summary: Shows the design decision to build AI Coach on AWS Lambda and Amazon Bedrock on-demand inference with Llama 3.3 70B, plus a translation layer that expanded legacy JSON keys and substituted safe defaults.

entry.title: Data Movement Strategies In System Design
entry.summary: The available text only outlined design choices among data movement strategies, listing pull, polling, push, long polling, SSE and WebSockets, message queues, change data capture and how to choose one.

entry.title: How DoorDash Reduced LLM Search Costs by 98% Without Losing Accuracy
entry.summary: Shows the design decision to decouple LLM search grounding from the model provider through an MCP-compatible gateway with exact and semantic caches and provider fallback, cutting QIU search cost by more than 98%.

entry.title: Catching Bugs Before They Land: JiTTesting’s Human-on-the-Loop Approach at Full Scale
entry.summary: Architecture walkthrough of Catching JiTTests, covering the dodgy diff and intent-aware test generation workflows, the LLM-as-Judge ensemble paired with the rule-based RubFake assessor, and the human-on-the-loop review design.

entry.title: Querying Databricks Apache Iceberg Tables with the borderless Lakehouse
entry.summary: Architecture walkthrough of zero-copy BigQuery reads of Databricks-managed Iceberg tables, covering Unity Catalog federation with credential vending, manifest-based partition pruning, metadata refresh as often as every 5 minutes, and compaction.

entry.title: Build Generative UI Apps with A2UI & CopilotKit Agents
entry.summary: Shows the trade-off between pre-built components and agent-written UI code for generative UI, and the A2UI choice of declarative JSON messages checked against a trusted client component catalog and streamed over AG-UI.

entry.title: How to Use AI Coding in Systems That Cannot Fail: Practice and Limits in Distributed Storage (translated from Chinese)
entry.summary: Meituan's storage team describes using AI for code review, debugging, a CMake build migration and an ARM port of a distributed KV store, and how tests and runtime logs verified AI findings.

entry.title: Unlocking Tensor Core Performance for Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials
entry.summary: Shows the precision versus throughput trade-off of running PET interatomic potential inference with BF16x9 and TF32x3 Tensor Core FP32 methods, reaching up to 1.7x MD-step speedups while preserving energy conservation.

entry.title: Measuring soft navigation web vitals
entry.summary: Architecture walkthrough of soft navigation web vitals in Sentry JavaScript SDK v11, covering why idle-based `navigation` spans miss user-visible timing, span streaming for late vitals, and the `browser.navigation.type` attribute.

entry.title: Software engineering at Google & CS education with Titus Winters
entry.summary: Shows the process decision to require a test with every change after Search slowed to quarterly releases, and the parse, match, coexist, shard and delete steps of a roughly 250M-line C++ refactor.

entry.title: Adaptive Integer Compression in TimescaleDB: Built for the Read Path
entry.summary: TimescaleDB introduces Adaptive Integer Compression, which picks a fast-decoding encoding per block of up to 256 values, giving about 10% smaller databases and around 50% faster typical queries.

entry.title: Upgrading MLflow Pipelines Across a Python Version Boundary
entry.summary: Shows the design decision to recover cloudpickle-serialized MLflow models broken by the Python 3.10 to 3.12 upgrade through a Load and Repack migration instead of retraining, and the planned move to native serialization formats.

entry.title: Automating agentic AI Well-Architected reviews with the AWS Agentic AI Lens
entry.summary: Smarsh built a Claude skill that reviews an agentic workload against 150 AWS Agentic AI Lens best practices, using a JSON dataset, an evidence rubric and a deterministic workbook generator.

entry.title: How Revinate accelerated API adoption with Amazon API Gateway
entry.summary: Revinate explains why it chose Amazon API Gateway and its portal over self-managed or enterprise gateways, and why it connected to EKS using TargetGroupBinding with Network Load Balancer target groups.

entry.title: How Uber Built A Gateway For AI Agents To Access Tools
entry.summary: The article explains how Uber built an MCP Gateway with a registry, a proxy that translates to HTTP, gRPC and TChannel, AutoCrawler tool discovery, tool-level access control and context-saving features.

entry.title: Adopting Cloud SQL Backup Vault to meet strict backup requirements (DeNA Infra SRE) (translated from Japanese)
entry.summary: DeNA describes adopting Cloud SQL Backup Vault with a cross-project setup for immutable backups, estimating about 77% lower monthly cost than daily GCS exports and noting plan and billing limits.

entry.title: 2026 Summer Engineering Intern Projects – Part One
entry.summary: Summarizes three summer 2026 intern projects on trustworthy LLM systems: a data-quality check suggester, an agent that builds dashboards, and an automated root cause analysis pipeline for multi-agent failures.

entry.title: Meta Andromeda: Powering the Next Generation of Ads Retrieval Through Model-System Co-Design
entry.summary: Meta describes the next Andromeda ads retrieval system, using a mixture-of-experts gating model, a fused GPU kernel and single-GPU co-location to score over one billion ads per second per server.

entry.title: Behind the scenes, two months later: How we ship Google Agent Skills like products
entry.summary: Google describes the pull request pipeline for its Agent Skills repository, with linters, semantic versioning checks, eval-suite validation, link checks, an AI review agent and human approval.

entry.title: How GKE networking scales to support high densities of concurrent AI agents
entry.summary: Google explains how moving high-cardinality pod labels to annotations and filtering labels in GKE Dataplane V2 avoids the 65,536 Cilium identity limit for high-density agent sandboxes.

entry.title: Hill-Climbing Agent Quality with Agents CLI Evaluation
entry.summary: A walkthrough of the Agents CLI eval commands on a LangChain agent, covering baseline scoring, a prompt regression, a model swap, nightly scheduled runs, threshold alerts and prompt optimization.

entry.title: Agentic harnesses (epilogue): working day to day with a frontier agent (translated from French)
entry.summary: The epilogue of an OCTO series describes a Claude Code workflow of agent interviews, Opus planning and Sonnet implementation, plus methods to re-audit the harness and reduce token use.

entry.title: A JSON schema Is not an AI governance layer
entry.summary: The author of the PIC protocol explains how duplicate identifiers, input normalization and self-asserted trust made agent action verifiers disagree, and proposes schema, semantic and policy layers with conformance vectors.

entry.title: How Anchorage Digital and Turnkey verify code with AWS Nitro Enclaves
entry.summary: Anchorage Digital and Turnkey run the VisualSign transaction parser inside AWS Nitro Enclaves so wallets can verify through attestation and reproducible builds which code parsed a transaction.

entry.title: Vessel-specific voyage optimization with machine learning: Manta on AWS
entry.summary: Manta Marine Technologies trains a model per vessel on AWS, using Airflow to run ETL, training and voyage optimization as ECS tasks on EC2 with per-instance-type capacity providers.

entry.title: How Apple Fits an LLM on Your iPhone
entry.summary: A summary of how Apple runs a 3-billion-parameter model on the iPhone using palettization, quantization-aware training, cross-layer KV sharing, LoRA adapters and Private Cloud Compute.

entry.title: From spot fixes to measured gains: improving document extraction accuracy with ai_extract and MLflow Prompt Registry
entry.summary: Databricks describes improving ai_extract accuracy on about 40 fields by versioning prompts and schemas in MLflow Prompt Registry and scoring candidates against reviewer-approved ground truth, cutting errors by 32%.

entry.title: How to make postMessage type-safe in under 350 bytes
entry.summary: Evil Martians describes typed-channel, a 271-byte library that makes postMessage, event buses and Figma plugin messaging type-safe, and its 0.11 request API with AbortSignal cancellation.

entry.title: Beyond the Prompt: Engineering the Loop for Software Change at Scale
entry.summary: Expedia Group describes an agent loop built on a Modularization MCP server, deterministic scripts, build and test gates and persistent memory that modularized its Shared iOS Components Stack in about three months.

entry.title: PrivacyLib: Privacy Controls at the Data Access Boundary
entry.summary: Meta describes PrivacyLib, a library inside the clients of hundreds of data systems that runs privacy modules such as Policy Zones on billions of checks per second, including agent tool calls.

entry.title: Securely connecting Gemini Enterprise to Snowflake data
entry.summary: A guide to connecting a Gemini Enterprise agent built with Google ADK to a Snowflake Cortex Agent over MCP, running queries with each user's OAuth session and role.

entry.title: Building Conversational Commerce with Multi-Agent Swarms on GCP: A Working Prototype
entry.summary: The HappyDelivery prototype implements conversational grocery ordering with a Pub/Sub-backed webhook ingress, a Redis session store and a LangGraph agent swarm on Gemini, reporting latency figures and about 4,240 tokens per session.

entry.title: Fast, reliable A2UI, with swappable inference formats
entry.summary: Google introduces swappable inference formats for A2UI, making the Python-like A2UI Express the default after comparing four formats, and shows the Jev decision model building fixed-layout screens in the Apparite example.

entry.title: How Spec-Driven Development Shaped My New Way of Engineering
entry.summary: A Gusto engineer describes adopting spec-driven development with AI agents, moving from spec-kit to OpenSpec, and adding a reviewer agent that scores spec and implementation alignment before pull requests.

entry.title: [Intern report] Re-architecting the Settlement Service that supports merchant settlement (translated from Japanese)
entry.summary: An intern describes the Settlement Service v1 to v2 re-architecture and the design of Transaction Clearing, which uses idempotency keys, ordered side effects, error detection and the Magician workflow engine for retries.

entry.title: 3 Ways to Boost MoE Inference on NVIDIA DGX Spark
entry.summary: NVIDIA shows how Humming MoE kernels, FP8 LM-head quantization and MTP speculative decoding raised Ling-3.0-flash decode throughput by 42.5% on GSM8K on a DGX Spark.

entry.title: Fine-Tuning NVIDIA Nemotron to Know Local Rules, Not Just Local Languages
entry.summary: NVIDIA shows how to fine-tune Nemotron 3.5 Lightning with LoRA on synthetic conversations from Nemotron-Personas-France to build a French public-service support agent and evaluate it.

entry.title: Memory-Enforced GPU Sharing in Kubernetes with NVIDIA CUDA 13.4
entry.summary: NVIDIA introduces the open-source gpu-fractioning operator and KAI Scheduler NvFractions mode, which use CUDA 13.4 to enforce per-workload GPU memory limits and compute modes in Kubernetes.

entry.title: What happened with npm packages over the last 12 months? (translated from French)
entry.summary: A French article reviewing npm supply chain attacks from August 2025 to August 2026 and proposing release-age delays, install-script blocking, CI secret separation and OIDC publishing.

entry.title: How a beagle-shaped AI agent ships code to madewithvuejs.com
entry.summary: The madewithvuejs.com team describes Milly, an AI agent with access to GitHub, Linear, Sentry and Discord that scouts content, builds features and fixed production bugs under defined safeguards.

entry.title: Freight Search: Composing a Shared Search Index from Independently Owned Fragments
entry.summary: Uber Freight explains Freight Search, which builds OpenSearch indices from fragments owned by separate data sources, ingesting over 70 topics into 300 fragments with Spark bootstrap and Flink CDC.

entry.title: Data governance with annotations in Amazon S3
entry.summary: An AWS reference design for keeping classification, retention, residency and PII context as Amazon S3 annotations, written by a Lambda and Bedrock pipeline and queried through an S3 Metadata annotation table with Athena.

entry.title: Recommended resilience testing in the next generation of AWS Resilience Hub
entry.summary: AWS introduces recommended resilience testing in Resilience Hub, four FIS-based tests including dependency validation, which uses DNS-based dependency discovery and packet loss injection to check soft and hard dependencies.

entry.title: A Deep Dive into Salesforce’s Agent Tech Stack
entry.summary: Salesforce replaced a single-prompt Agentforce design with Agent Script, Data 360 identity resolution, the Agent Context Engine and Agent Identity, and exposed its platform to outside agents through AIforce and an MCP server.

entry.title: Cross-request KV cache exposure in the GLM-5.3 Workers AI model, and our remediation with SGLang
entry.summary: Cloudflare explains how a prefill KV cache pool smaller than the context window and an SGLang disaggregation bug let 155 GLM 5.3 responses on Workers AI include other users' data, and the fixes that followed.

entry.title: Easy to integrate, compliant by design: Bringing the Swiss Franc to Google Cloud Universal Ledger
entry.summary: Crypto Finance Group and Google Cloud describe a pilot on Google Cloud Universal Ledger enabling instant transfers between customers of two Swiss banks, using deferred settlement and integration completed in under three months.

entry.title: Scale agents securely with IAM Helper Agent Skills and MCP Tools
entry.summary: Google Cloud introduces IAM Helper, Agent Skills and Google-managed MCP tools that let coding agents troubleshoot 403 errors, author policies, simulate changes against 90 days of logs and request just-in-time access.

entry.title: Unifying enterprise context and semantics: LookML in Knowledge Catalog is now GA
entry.summary: Google Cloud announces general availability of LookML semantic indexing in Knowledge Catalog, so Gemini Enterprise and custom agents can use indexed join paths, metric formulas and lineage when generating SQL.

entry.title: Making Failure Diagnosis Reliable with Pensive AI
entry.summary: Netflix describes Pensive AI, which adds LLM error extraction by line ranges and on-demand cached debugging to its rule-based failure diagnosis system, reaching extraction coverage of 100% of failed workloads.

entry.title: Multi‑Ratio Video Resizing for Mobile Feed and Marketing
entry.summary: Netflix describes an automated system that crops 16:9 video into 9:16, 4:5 and 1:1 variants using shot detection, active speaker detection, saliency and temporal smoothing, integrated into its Clips tool.

entry.title: How NVIDIA Minerva Turns Telemetry Chaos Into Peak GPU Yield
entry.summary: NVIDIA Minerva is an AIOps platform that maps AI factory infrastructure to jobs in a knowledge graph, detects gray failures with machine learning, correlates alert storms into incidents and offers the Sherlock agent.

entry.title: How NVIDIA Mission Control 2.5 Brings Autonomous Recovery to Kubernetes
entry.summary: NVIDIA Mission Control 2.5 extends its autonomous recovery engine from Slurm to Kubernetes workloads under NVIDIA Run:ai, combining scheduler placement, job recovery and hardware recovery to handle hardware faults and transient errors.

entry.title: Agentic harnesses (2/2): eight reflexes to unlearn for a frugal harness (translated from French)
entry.summary: A French guide to eight habits to unlearn when building agent harnesses for Claude Code, covering concise instructions, Tool Search, effort levels, total task cost, prompt caching, high-level tools, restarts and context compaction.

entry.title: Advancing Generative Recommendation Inference: our collaboration with NVIDIA on TensorRT LLM
entry.summary: Spotify describes moving generative recommendation inference from vLLM and SGLang to TensorRT LLM with NVIDIA, adding beam search, scoring and soft-token features, with up to 54% cost reduction for beam search.

entry.title: AI Changed How Spotify Builds. What We Learned (and Fixed) About Quality at Higher Velocity
entry.summary: Spotify describes quality problems during its shift to AI-assisted development, including a June 24 publishing delay and failover capacity issues, the fixes it made, and incident and pull request data on AI impact.

entry.title: Indexing the Data Lake for Online Point Queries
entry.summary: Spotify describes Random Access Parquet, an external index mapping keys to Parquet files and rows so online services and AI agents can run fast point queries over its GCS data lake.

entry.title: Portal by Spotify cut my Claude Code token usage by 90%
entry.summary: A Spotify engineer describes the shunt Claude Code plugin and two AiKA Modes in Portal that route bulk file reads and boilerplate code to Gemini 2.5 Flash, saving around 90% of bulk-read tokens.

entry.title: When Can LLMs Replace Humans in A/B Tests?
entry.summary: A paper summary on when LLM predictions can replace human outcomes in A/B tests, defining surrogacy and comparability conditions and testing gpt-4o-mini calibration methods on the Upworthy Research Archive.

entry.title: Why Spotify Is Not Using Bayesian A/B Testing
entry.summary: Spotify examined common claims about Bayesian A/B testing, compared Bayesian configurations with frequentist ones, and explained why its experimentation program kept only frequentist inference rather than adding a Bayesian mode.

entry.title: GHARP: Real-Time Gaussian Head Animation from Large-Scale Reconstruction Prior
entry.summary: A research abstract presenting GHARP, a two-stage method that animates 3D Gaussian heads in real time from a few images, reporting state-of-the-art quality on Ava-256 and up to 13× faster runtime on an A100.

entry.title: Genie One MCP: Give any AI Agent the Right Business Context
entry.summary: Databricks introduces Genie One MCP, which exposes Genie One and the Genie Ontology context layer to MCP-compatible assistants through five tools, with on-behalf-of user authentication and Unity Catalog permission enforcement.

entry.title: The challenge of building an exploit-strategy AI for EDGE POKER (translated from Japanese)
entry.summary: A DeNA intern builds an exploit-strategy AI for six-player poker in EDGE POKER by adding an MLP to the frozen EDGE AI model, raising simulated profit from +27.1 to +52.9 bb/100.

entry.title: Background Coding Agents: Supercharging Downstream Consumer Dataset Migrations (Honk, Part 4)
entry.summary: Spotify used its Honk background coding agent with Backstage and Fleetshift to migrate consumers of two deprecated datasets, rolling out 240 automated PRs across dbt and BigQuery Runner pipelines.

entry.title: Better Experiments with LLM Evals — A funnel, not a fork
entry.summary: Spotify argues LLM evals belong before A/B tests in an evaluation funnel, citing that about 12% of its tests ship positive results and about 42% of launched experiments are rolled back.

entry.title: Building a Natural Language Interface to the Spotify Ads API with Claude Code Plugins
entry.summary: Spotify describes an open-source Claude Code plugin that turns natural language into Spotify Ads API v3 calls using Markdown skills, an agent, a PreToolUse hook and an approximately 8,600-line OpenAPI spec instead of MCP.

entry.title: Coding Is No Longer the Constraint: Scaling Developer Experience to Teams and Agents at Spotify
entry.summary: Spotify describes its Fleet Management system Fleetshift, its Claude-based background coding agent Honk, and Backstage standardization, citing more than 2.5 million automated maintenance PRs and a 76% increase in pull request frequency.

entry.title: Content Ingestion & Podcast Video Incident Report
entry.summary: Spotify reports on the June 24 video podcast publishing delay caused by transcoding capacity limits, a batch job and a scheduling bug, and the fixes including about 67% more transcoding capacity.

entry.title: Encoding Your Domain Expert: The Context Layer Behind Spotify's Data Assistant
entry.summary: Spotify describes the cluster-based context layer behind its Vedder data assistant, where domain experts curate datasets, question-SQL pairs and docs over 70,000+ datasets, with curators accepting only 12.5% of mined pairs.

entry.title: Bringing post-quantum cryptography to geographically fenced key management
entry.summary: Cloudflare launched a post-quantum GeoKey Manager in closed beta that wraps customer decryption keys so only servers in a chosen region can unwrap them, using hybrid ML-KEM-768 and X25519.

entry.title: Origin Range Requests: Serving large files without range-request tuning
entry.summary: Cloudflare rebuilt range-request caching on its Pingora-based cache to align origin fetches to disk chunks, roughly halving p99 time to first byte for R2 and cutting tiered cache traffic about 6%.

entry.title: Built for Agents: The Case for Spark Declarative Pipelines
entry.summary: Databricks benchmarked 528 agent-built data pipelines and found declarative Spark Declarative Pipelines cheaper, faster and leaner than procedural PySpark for coding agents.

entry.title: Beyond API Compatibility: Building a Tool to Measure the Blast Radius of Library Changes
entry.summary: Netflix's Java Platform team built Quasar, which indexes code from CI builds into Parquet on S3 to show which repositories use API symbols that a library change affects.

entry.title: Scaling NVIDIA TensorRT Performance Optimization Beyond a Single Build Route with the Global Performance Tuner, Part 1
entry.summary: Part 1 introduces the Global Performance Tuner in TensorRT 11.1, describing heuristic sprawl in default scheduling and a mathematical model of builder and search algorithms over accuracy-feasible solutions.

entry.title: Scaling NVIDIA TensorRT Performance Optimization Beyond a Single Build Route with the Global Performance Tuner, Part 2
entry.summary: NVIDIA describes the design of the TensorRT 11.1 Global Performance Tuner, which searches build routes of over 200 compiler knobs under an accuracy tolerance and gave 1.14x to 1.63x speedups on ten workloads.

entry.title: Using AI Agents to Teach Robots Like Microduck to Walk in Simulation
entry.summary: NVIDIA describes a workflow in which Hermes, Nemotron and Astra agents plan and build a Microduck obstacle course, Isaac Lab trains a navigation policy on 4,096 parallel environments, and Isaac Sim validates it.

entry.title: Agentic harnesses (1/2): why yesterday's good practices are expensive today (translated from French)
entry.summary: The article argues that coding-agent harness practices built for weaker models, such as long AGENTS.md files and maximum reasoning, now cost more, using token prices and prompt-cache behaviour as worked examples.

entry.title: My agents were reading too much: what ten weeks of token hunting taught me (translated from French)
entry.summary: A product coach measured the billable tokens of his AI agents and applied seven measures, such as a 150-line CLAUDE.md cap, after which median tokens per launched agent fell 55%.

entry.title: Rapidly scaling online storage to serve over 1 billion ChatGPT users (Part II)
entry.summary: OpenAI describes scaling its Habitat storage platform on Azure Cosmos DB through tenancy changes, hot-key throttling, CDC-invalidated Valkey caching and a Rust rewrite, cutting read p50 to roughly 10 ms.

entry.title: How Retention Policies Silently Break Continuous Aggregates
entry.summary: A TimescaleDB retention job that dropped raw chunks inside a continuous aggregate's refresh window made the next refresh silently delete buckets; the fix is one retention-versus-refresh invariant plus an audit query.

entry.title: Localizing compliance at scale: achieving South Korea’s ISMS certification
entry.summary: Cloudflare obtained South Korea's ISMS certification and, to enforce itemized consent, removed social sign-up in South Korea rather than build a separate consent gate after authentication.

entry.title: The AI Bill is coming
entry.summary: Databricks co-founder Patrick Wendell explains how AI coding agent costs spiraled at Databricks and how a central gateway, model routing and spend visibility cut unit costs by up to 90%.

entry.title: The Fraud Analyst AI Coworker: Detecting Telecom Fraud in Real-Time on One Platform
entry.summary: Databricks argues that telecom fraud signals are split across six or seven systems synced by batch jobs, and outlines a unified real-time architecture and AI analyst assistant.

entry.title: Dark mode was never on our roadmap. Here’s how it got built.
entry.summary: One Medium web engineer built dark mode using CSS light-dark() tokens instead of caching separate light and dark copies, with a Statsig flag splitting the Cloudflare Workers edge cache during rollout.

entry.title: Single-tenant Titus: VM-level isolation on a multi-tenant container platform
entry.summary: Netflix added an allowlisted single-tenant mode to its Titus container platform that gives a task its own right-sized EC2 instance, after weighing shared-kernel tuning, microVMs, gVisor and plain EC2.

entry.title: How to Read Data into GPU Memory in Python with NVIDIA GPUDirect Storage
entry.summary: A tutorial on reading data into GPU memory with the NVIDIA KvikIO Python API over GPUDirect Storage and cuFile, verifying the nvidia-fs path with gds_stats and explaining how a 1 GiB read is split.

entry.title: Running Frontier-Class AI Models Across 8 NVIDIA DGX Spark Nodes
entry.summary: NVIDIA announces eight-node DGX Spark clusters with 1 TB unified memory and benchmarks inference, the RoCEnante collective backend, ring versus switch topologies, Switchyard model routing and nanochat pre-training scaling.

entry.title: We gave AI agents a mobile dev environment
entry.summary: Shopify built Remote Dev, a pool of warm remote Macs that AI agents claim over SSH to build and test its mobile apps, with Android emulators on separate Linux VMs.

entry.title: We built three memory systems. The most expressive one wasn’t the most useful.
entry.summary: Tiger Data built three memory systems for its Slack agent Eon, a fact list, a PostgreSQL knowledge graph and an ltree tree with hybrid search, and kept the tree.

entry.title: Automate medical coding with Step Functions and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
entry.summary: AWS shows a medical coding pipeline using Step Functions, Lambda, an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness and Aurora pgvector, which autocoded confident terms and sent cases below a 0.90 confidence gate to human coders.

entry.title: Cloudflare deploys protections against php2shell vulnerability
entry.summary: Cloudflare deployed WAF protections against the php2shell PHP vulnerabilities about 9 hours before public disclosure, using full transaction detection that combines request and origin-response signals.

entry.title: How Commerce.com and Cloudflare are getting storefronts ready for AI agents
entry.summary: Commerce.com and Cloudflare enabled WebMCP agent tools across almost 100,000 storefronts with a per-merchant opt-out built from Configuration Rules and custom hostname metadata.

entry.title: Introducing full transaction detection for Cloudflare WAF
entry.summary: Cloudflare added full transaction detection to its WAF, evaluating each request together with the origin's response, and response rules that can block a matching response.

entry.title: Aligning Dispatch to Reality: Using Reinforcement Learning to Adapt Real-Time Objective Weight
entry.summary: Describes an offline-trained reinforcement learning policy that adjusts a dispatch objective-weight multiplier per store, tested in a global switchback experiment against the production optimizer.

entry.title: Achieve Productive AI Capacity Faster and More Predictably with NVIDIA DSX POD
entry.summary: NVIDIA describes the DSX POD reference design for Vera Rubin rack-scale systems, which pre-integrates and validates compute, networking, storage, 800 VDC power and liquid cooling in factory-built containers before site delivery.

entry.title: Design Proteins with RFD4-Proteina Using Reward-Guided Inference-Time Search
entry.summary: A tutorial on designing PD-L1 protein binders with NVIDIA RFD4-Proteina through the open model and a NIM microservice, using reward-guided inference-time search scored by OpenFold3 pLDDT.

entry.title: Developing an AI Factory Digital Twin with an Agent-Assisted Workflow
entry.summary: NVIDIA describes an agent-assisted workflow that turns DSX Blueprint assets, site plans and USGS geographic data into an editable OpenUSD AI factory campus model and proposes a fixed-power capacity study.

entry.title: How NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture Secures and Governs AI Agent Workloads at Scale
entry.summary: NVIDIA describes the OpenShell reference architecture, with gateway, supervisor, sandbox and policy prover components, running on Vera CPUs with optional NVIDIA Sentry on BlueField-4 DPUs for hardware-enforced agent governance.

entry.title: Inside NVIDIA Sentry: Secure AI Agents at Runtime
entry.summary: NVIDIA describes Sentry, a BlueField-4 based framework that uses DOCA Flow, the Envoy-based DOCA Tower proxy with Open Policy Agent, and DOCA Argus memory introspection to monitor and contain AI agents.

entry.title: How we built ChatGPT’s novel ad stack for user trust and relevance
entry.summary: OpenAI describes the ChatGPT ads stack: stateful ads sessions, a post-trained LLM orchestrator calling retrieval, filtering, scoring and auction tools, and an ads service separate from answer generation.

entry.title: Designing IIoT Ingest That Survives a Cut Uplink
entry.summary: A guide to an IIoT ingest path in PostgreSQL that replays buffered rows exactly once after an outage, using a unique constraint, a SQLite buffer and a rate-capped COPY replay.

entry.title: 8 eMudhra certificates are compromised. Here's what you need to know
entry.summary: Cloudflare describes its response after private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate certificates were compromised, including trust-store updates and CDN and Zero Trust mitigations deployed on October 20.

entry.title: Introducing tsrs: A port of TypeScript to Rust
entry.summary: Cloudflare, VoidZero and Owner.com are building tsrs, a faithful Rust port of the TypeScript compiler that is up to 8x faster and uses about 70% less memory than TypeScript 7.0.

entry.title: How DoorDash Built a Next-Generation Real-Time Dispatch Platform
entry.summary: Describes how DoorDash replaced a monolithic dispatch engine with a coordinator and distributed compute tier, reporting ten-fold throughput and more than 99.96% of runs finishing in under 20 seconds.

entry.title: The Agents on Rails Files: designing black-box evals for coding agents
entry.summary: Evil Martians replaced hidden Rails tests with browser-based black-box checks for stage 3 of their Agents on Rails coding-agent benchmark and calibrated the grader with mutants.

entry.title: The Quiet Tax on Machine Learning Teams
entry.summary: Expedia Group built a CLI that scaffolds ML projects per business domain and copies shared infrastructure code into each project, to stop repeating CI/CD, permission and cluster setup for every model.

entry.title: How 3 Java Champions are using GitHub Copilot for increased productivity
entry.summary: Three Java Champions describe using GitHub Copilot, including migrating about 900 slides from Reveal.js to Marp and diagnosing a Pi4J virtual-thread pinning bug on a Raspberry Pi 4.

entry.title: App stability at scale with a layered defense
